s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent vertical misalignment with elevation deficit
salient_findings: Elevation deficit of the right eye
Anomalous band in the right orbit
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle
key_facts: 52-year-old woman
History of long-standing diplopia
Persistent vertical misalignment
Orthotropic in primary position
Elevation deficit of the right eye
Previous MRI of the orbits revealed an anomalous band in the right orbit
Surgical excision of the anomalous band did not improve motility
Diplopia remained stable in primary gaze
MRI of the orbits with and without gadolinium was obtained in 2023
Globes were unremarkable with no measured proptosis
Retroocular fat, optic nerves and sheaths, optic chiasm, and brain parenchyma appeared normal
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion was noted medial to the medial rectus muscle

shortlist.label: Brown syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of persistent vertical misalignment with elevation deficit

shortlist.label: Superior oblique tendon syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the patient's history of diplopia and elevation deficit

shortlist.label: Monocular elevation deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Explains the patient's inability to elevate the right eye

shortlist.label: Adhesive syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the anomalous band in the right orbit and persistent diplopia

shortlist.label: Anomalous extraocular muscle
shortlist.why_kept: Correlates with the MRI finding of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion with signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle
